description: Two independent envelope generators, each switchable between ADSR, AR and a free-running LFO

params.text: Sets the attack time, the climb from 0V to 10V; fully counter-clockwise is the fastest and fully clockwise the slowest
Sets the fall from the peak down to the S level, and only when the mode switch is at ADSR; fully counter-clockwise is the fastest
Sets the level the envelope holds while the gate is high in ADSR mode, 0V at fully counter-clockwise and a shade under 10V at fully clockwise; moving it during the hold moves the output at once
Sets the fall back to 0V: after the gate goes low in ADSR mode, and straight down from the peak in AR and LFO modes; fully counter-clockwise is the fastest
Switched up to ADSR the envelope attacks, decays to the S level, holds while the gate is high and releases; at AR a gate starts an attack and release that runs to its own end; at LFO the two repeat

inputs.text: A gate above 1V starts the envelope; in ADSR mode it releases when the gate goes low, in AR mode the cycle finishes regardless, and in LFO mode the gate starts the LFO and going low stops it

outputs.text: The envelope, 0V to 10V, generated at 1kHz and smoothed by a one-pole filter on the way out

notes: in LFO mode the LFO free-runs as soon as the mode switch reaches LFO, but a gate at GATE IN takes that over and starts and stops it. Switching the mode away and back restores free running.
the envelopes are generated at 1kHz, so a very fast attack or decay steps rather than glides. That is a deliberate part of the clone of the microcontroller hardware.

inputs.0:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
